_readme: CURATED, not derived. Figures published by a named authority that this
channel cites rather than measures. T10 is cite-never-author, and citing
somebody else's number is a different act from producing one.
Every entry MUST carry: the exact quantity it measures, who said it, when,
and a link. A cited figure with no quantity is the dangerous case, because
a reader assumes it is the same quantity as the measured number beside it.
quantity is the field that stops a false comparison. 'area_affected' and
'area_burnt' are DIFFERENT MEASUREMENTS: affected is normally the
perimeter, and the burnt area inside it is smaller. EFFIS maps burnt area.
So a later EFFIS figure BELOW a cited affected figure is not a correction
and must never be reported as one.
Entries are removed when the authoritative series catches up, not kept as

BEL.quantity_note: Area AFFECTED by the fire, which is not the same as area burnt. The source says 'superficie concernee', not 'superficie brulee'. Affected is normally the perimeter; burnt area inside it is smaller. EFFIS maps burnt area, so an EFFIS figure below 3,000 would not contradict this.
BEL.wording: La superficie concernee par l'incendie est actuellement estimee a 3 000 hectares
BEL.verified_by: fire chat, against the primary source, 2026-08-17
BEL.display_rule: Show beside the measured burnt-area figure, never instead of it, and never subtract or compare the two as if they were the same quantity. Both carry their own date. The gap between them is the latency story and should be stated rather than hidden.
BEL.retire_when: EFFIS publishes week 33 for Belgium, expected around 2026-08-19
